Keep track of the change

CodeRabbit Change Stack · Formbricks #8650 · Parth Pawar

Make Change Stack easier to review without losing what it can do. I focused on understanding a change, checking its code and keeping track of the review. My starting assumption: as a PR grows, holding the layer, file, explanation and review state together becomes extra work.

What I noticedWhat I chose, and why
Summary points share a broad range. Expanding also moves the code.Expand in place, with explicit links to individual statements. Reading and navigation become separate actions. The full wording and whole function remain available.
Layers and files are separate. Following a guard leaves a return trip to remember.Nest files under their layer. Inspect guard opens the dependency; Return restores the caller and position. This keeps one wide code pane; a side-by-side option would need more horizontal space.
Actions span several groups. Seen, viewed and submitted mean different things.Keep frequent file actions beside the filename and secondary actions in Tools. Mark viewed updates file progress with Undo. Reading a summary never marks the file reviewed.
Message totals, severity and resolution can be read as one signal.Group comments by resolution, with severity on the finding and replies inside its thread. A resolved Major finding reads as history. Show source messages separately from captured threads and local notes.

What I gave up

The original fits more code. This iteration gives files and explanations more room; Focus returns that space to the diff. Smaller highlights may draw attention away from a relevant branch. Inspect + Return also means switching views instead of seeing both files together.

What I kept

The original PR header arrangement, merged state, layer order, complexity labels, J/K and Focus remain. Gray marks navigation and display selection; orange connects a statement to code. The original already has severity and resolved filters; my change is the reading order, not a new capability.

What I would test

Ask developers to explain this access check on both screens, inspect its guard and return, then find a branch the summary misses. Check whether a resolved Major finding reads as history. I expect less searching and backtracking, but I have not measured that. Clearer Overview multi-select filters are a follow-up.

Observations and assumptions from using this PR, not developer research. Seven of 52 diffs at commit 23cdac2; manually mapped links; one paraphrased finding, with two reply bodies omitted. Secondary workflows are previews. Submit is disabled for the merged PR. Work exceeded the 1–2 hour brief. Paper requires sign-in.
